services.workflow.title: Project Development Stages
services.workflow.step1_desc: We assess your organic waste potential, analyze local substrate availability, and precisely calculate the return on investment for your future biogas plant.
services.workflow.step2_desc: Our engineering team designs anaerobic digestion systems optimized specifically for your waste type, ensuring maximum operational efficiency and structural durability.

services.workflow.step4_desc: We provide 24/7 remote monitoring, regular biological analysis, and technical maintenance to keep your plant running at peak performance with zero downtime.
services.faq.title: Common Technical Questions
services.faq.q1: How do Iona mixing systems maximize biogas yield?
services.faq.a1: Our advanced vertical and horizontal agitation technologies eliminate dead zones and prevent foam formation. This ensures excellent substrate homogeneity, delivering maximum methane conversion and higher energy efficiency.
services.faq.q2: Can your systems handle high dry matter content?
services.faq.a2: Yes. With Iona's proprietary mixing technology and robust direct solids feeding systems, our plants maintain highly stable operation even at dry matter content of up to 14% within the anaerobic digester.
services.faq.q3: How does the zero-energy overflow system work?
services.faq.a3: Our innovative Overflow Transfer System (OFT) operates entirely on the "connected vessels" principle. By intelligently harnessing gravity for digestate transfer, it greatly reduces mechanical stress and cuts pumping energy consumption by up to 66%.
services.faq.q4: What protects pipelines from freezing in winter?
services.faq.a4: Every Iona plant includes automatic thermal Freeze Protection integrated with smart sensors. The system automatically detects sub-zero ambient temperatures and activates line heating to prevent freezing and avoid costly downtime.

flux.hero.title: Know what is happening at your plant, as it happens.
flux.hero.body: IonaFlux is the application IONA hands over to the operator together with the plant it builds. Production, feeding, laboratory, fault and field records sit in one place on your phone and computer, and IONA's engineers look at the same data.
flux.live.title: On automated plants, values arrive live.
flux.live.body: Where the plant's PLC is connected to the panel, temperature, flow, level and equipment status appear live. When a value leaves its limits, the responsible person is notified, so a problem at night does not wait for the morning report.
flux.catalog.title: What you can do
flux.catalog.item1_desc: Download daily field, production and analysis reports as PDF and share them directly with partners and financiers.
flux.catalog.item2_desc: Open a fault from the field with a photo; it is assigned to the right person and tracked through open, assigned, in progress and resolved. Resolved faults build up a knowledge base.
flux.catalog.item3_desc: Shift plans, task assignment, checklists, weighbridge, logistics trips and feeding recipes in the same application.
flux.qr.title: The equipment's history, in the QR code on it.
flux.qr.body: Scan the QR code on a piece of equipment with a phone to open its serial number, technical documents, and maintenance and fault history. The field team no longer has to describe which part they mean.
flux.lab.title: When yield drops, see why.
flux.lab.body: Laboratory results sit next to feeding and production data. The digester health score shows which value has left its range, and you can estimate the effect of a change in the feeding recipe on production in advance.
flux.fleet.title: Fewer phone calls, earlier decisions.
flux.fleet.body: IonaFlux does not run the plant for you; it puts the information you need in front of you so you can make the right call earlier.
flux.video.title: Watch IonaFlux in Two Minutes.
flux.video.body: A short walkthrough with real screens, showing the app exactly as it's delivered to our customers.

svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.title: Biogas Plant Design and Process Engineering
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.lead: A biogas plant designed around your feedstock, your site and the energy you want to produce, with biology, mechanical, electrical and civil works treated as one process.
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.alt: Exterior of a digester tank at a biogas plant
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.item1: Feedstock analysis: composition, biodegradability and expected gas yield of the organic matter.
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.item2: Anaerobic digester design: hydraulic retention time (HRT), organic loading rate (OLR), mesophilic or thermophilic regime and the mixing layout.
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.item3: Integrated process flow: pre-treatment, digester, gas storage, gas treatment, CHP and digestate handling laid out to work as one system.
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.item4: Material selection, corrosion protection and thermal insulation.
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.item5: Automation and monitoring: controls that keep conditions stable, flag deviations early and support remote operation and data logging.
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.item6: Environmental requirements: gas-tight construction, odour management and digestate valorisation.
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.faq.q1: Where does biogas plant design start?
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.faq.a1: With the feedstock. Digester volume, mixing and the gas line cannot be sized correctly until you know which waste arrives, in what quantity and on what schedule. Mapping the feed profile is always the first step.
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.faq.q2: Should the plant run mesophilic or thermophilic?
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.faq.a2: It depends on the feedstock, hygiene requirements and ease of operation. A mesophilic regime is more stable and easier to run; a thermophilic regime breaks material down faster but needs tighter temperature control.
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.faq.q3: Should the plant produce electricity or biomethane?
svc.biyogaz_tesisi_tasarimi.faq.a3: That depends on the grid connection, heat use and the option to sell gas. The design follows that decision with either a CHP or a gas upgrading line; we weigh it together at the feasibility stage.
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.title: Turnkey (EPC) Biogas Plant Construction
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.lead: We bring engineering, procurement and construction under one contract, so a single party is responsible for the whole plant from feasibility to commissioning.
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.alt: Digester reactor being assembled on site
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.item1: Project management: we run every stage and shape the plant around your operational needs.
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.item2: Engineering: detailed design and system optimisation so the digester, gas line and CHP work together efficiently.
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.item3: Procurement: selecting and sourcing equipment and materials that meet technical and regulatory requirements.
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.item4: Construction and installation: site preparation, concrete works, equipment installation, process piping, electrical and automation, with safety and quality supervision on our side.
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.item5: Commissioning: inoculation, first gas production, testing and tuning of every system.
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.item6: Training and support: training for plant staff and technical support after handover.
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.faq.a1: Engineering, equipment procurement and construction are the responsibility of a single contractor. The investor does not coordinate separate subcontractors and receives a working plant at handover.
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.faq.a2: Staff are trained, the plant is monitored remotely and technical support continues. If you like, you can follow the plant's operation on one screen with IonaFlux.
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.faq.q3: Can you deliver EPC on an existing design?
svc.anahtar_teslim_epc.faq.a3: Yes. We take over another firm's design, review it, correct it where needed and carry out construction.
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.title: Optimisation and Re-engineering of Existing Biogas Plants
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.lead: We examine plants that run but do not deliver the expected output, find the root cause and make the necessary changes.
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.alt: Inside of a digester showing the mixing layout
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.item1: Diagnostics: on-site review of the digester, mixing, gas line, CHP and digestate handling.
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.item2: Analysis: operating data and process calculations to locate losses in energy production, heat recovery and feed management.
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.item3: Biological review: feeding pattern, organic load and process stability.
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.item4: Modifications: equipment retrofits, improved mixing and feeding, updated control logic.
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.item5: Additional units: adding missing links such as gas storage, odour control or gas treatment.
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.faq.q1: Why does an existing plant lose efficiency?
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.faq.a1: The most common causes are changes in the feed, insufficient mixing and sediment build-up, temperature fluctuations and losses in the gas line. Several causes often act together, which is why we look at the plant as a whole.
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.faq.q2: Do you work on plants built by other companies?
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.faq.a2: Yes. We review and re-engineer plants regardless of who built them.
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.faq.q3: Does the plant have to stop for optimisation?
svc.tesis_optimizasyonu.faq.a3: Most of the review is done while the plant is running. If equipment has to be changed, we plan it to keep downtime as short as possible.
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.title: Gas Purification and Biomethane Units
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.lead: Treatment lines that make raw biogas fit for an engine or the grid: moisture removal, H₂S removal and, where needed, CO₂ separation to produce biomethane.
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.alt: Gas analyser at a biogas plant
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.item1: Moisture removal: taking water out of the gas by cooling and expansion.
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.item2: H₂S removal: removing sulphur compounds to protect engines and equipment from corrosion.
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.item3: Activated carbon filters: capturing trace contaminants such as H₂S, siloxanes and VOCs, with media monitoring and replacement planned in.
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.item4: Absorption units: CO₂ and H₂S separation by water scrubbing (physical) or amines (chemical), for projects targeting grid-quality biomethane.
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.item5: Site-specific selection: the treatment method is chosen for the feedstock, the gas end use and the operating conditions.
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.faq.a1: Hydrogen sulphide forms acids with moisture and corrodes engines, pipes and equipment; when burned it also produces sulphur oxide emissions. Removing it before the gas is used is essential for equipment life and emission limits.
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.faq.q2: What is the difference between biogas and biomethane?
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.faq.a2: Biogas is the raw mixture of methane and carbon dioxide that leaves the digester. Biomethane is gas brought up to natural-gas quality by separating CO₂ and contaminants; it can be injected into the grid or used as vehicle fuel.
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.faq.q3: Which treatment is enough for an engine?
svc.gaz_aritma_biyometan.faq.a3: For CHP engines, moisture and H₂S removal, plus activated carbon where needed, is usually enough. The final choice depends on the gas analysis and the engine maker's gas quality requirements.
svc.digestat_ayirma.title: Digestate Separation and Enrichment
svc.digestat_ayirma.lead: We split the digestate leaving the digester into solid and liquid fractions and turn it into a product that can be transported, stored and used as fertiliser.
svc.digestat_ayirma.alt: Process equipment at a biogas plant
svc.digestat_ayirma.item1: Solid-liquid separation: mechanical separation with a screw press or centrifuge.
svc.digestat_ayirma.item2: Dewatering the liquid fraction: belt press or centrifuge to make handling and storage easier.
svc.digestat_ayirma.item3: Enrichment: adjusting the nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium balance to the need.
svc.digestat_ayirma.item4: Stabilisation: composting or thermal hygienisation of the solid fraction.
svc.digestat_ayirma.item5: End product: drying or pelleting into a marketable organic fertiliser or soil improver.
svc.digestat_ayirma.faq.a1: It is the nutrient-rich residue that leaves the digester after biogas has been produced. Processed correctly, it can be used as organic fertiliser and soil improver.
svc.digestat_ayirma.faq.a2: Separating solids and liquids reduces volume and makes storage and transport easier; the solid fraction is processed into fertiliser while the liquid can be used for irrigation or recirculation.
svc.digestat_ayirma.faq.q3: Which separation method should be used?
svc.digestat_ayirma.faq.a3: A screw press, centrifuge or belt press is chosen according to the digestate's dry matter content, fibre structure and where the product will be used.
svc.kurutma_uniteleri.title: Drying Units
svc.kurutma_uniteleri.lead: Units that dry digestate, manure and sewage sludge to cut volume and make storage and sale easier, using the plant's own waste heat wherever possible.
svc.kurutma_uniteleri.alt: Heat recovery line in an engine room
svc.kurutma_uniteleri.item1: Organic fertiliser drying: rotary drum, belt or fluidised bed dryers for manure, agricultural residues and biowaste.
svc.kurutma_uniteleri.item2: Sludge drying: low-temperature belt, solar or thermal drying for municipal and industrial sewage sludge.
svc.kurutma_uniteleri.item3: Heat integration: using waste heat from the CHP for drying.
svc.kurutma_uniteleri.item4: Odour control: treating the dryer exhaust air.
svc.kurutma_uniteleri.item5: Product preparation: getting the dried material ready for pelleting or bagging.
svc.kurutma_uniteleri.faq.a1: Drying lowers the water content, reducing volume and transport cost, and makes the product storable and saleable for longer.
svc.kurutma_uniteleri.faq.a2: At biogas plants, waste heat from the CHP engines can often be used for drying. The heat balance is calculated at the design stage.
svc.kurutma_uniteleri.faq.a3: Dryer exhaust air can carry odour, so odour removal equipment such as a biofilter or scrubber is included in the design.
svc.koku_giderme.title: Odour Removal Units
svc.koku_giderme.lead: Systems sized to air flow and pollutant load that treat odorous air from the reception, pre-treatment and drying areas of biogas and bioenergy plants.
svc.koku_giderme.alt: Aerial view of a biogas plant
svc.koku_giderme.item1: Biofilters: biological treatment on media such as compost, peat or wood chips, for continuous, low-concentration odours.
svc.koku_giderme.item2: Chemical scrubbers: acidic or alkaline solutions that capture ammonia and hydrogen sulphide.
svc.koku_giderme.item3: Activated carbon filters: a final polishing step that captures remaining odorous compounds before release.
svc.koku_giderme.item4: Sizing: system selection based on air flow, pollutant load and the required removal level.
svc.koku_giderme.item5: Control at source: enclosed reception areas and well-placed extraction points.
svc.koku_giderme.faq.a1: Digestion takes place in closed tanks, so odour mostly comes from the areas where feedstock is received and prepared and where digestate is handled. Enclosing these areas and treating their air brings odour largely under control.
svc.koku_giderme.faq.q2: Which odour removal method should be used?
svc.koku_giderme.faq.a2: It depends on the source, the air flow and the type of pollutant. Biofilters suit continuous low-concentration odours, chemical scrubbers suit air rich in ammonia or H₂S, and activated carbon can be added as a final step.
svc.koku_giderme.faq.q3: Can odour removal be added to an existing plant?
svc.koku_giderme.faq.a3: Yes. We identify the sources on site and design a system that fits the existing plant.
svc.substrat_hazirlama.title: Lignocellulosic Feedstock (Straw, Silage) Preparation
svc.substrat_hazirlama.lead: Pre-treatment that helps straw, silage and similar fibrous feedstocks break down better in the digester: the right particle size, the right moisture and a homogeneous feed.
svc.substrat_hazirlama.alt: Feed pool at a biogas plant
svc.substrat_hazirlama.item1: Physical pre-treatment: grinding, milling or shredding to reduce particle size.
svc.substrat_hazirlama.item2: Thermal and steam treatment: methods such as steam explosion that open up the fibre structure.
svc.substrat_hazirlama.item3: Chemical and biological pre-treatment: dilute acid/alkali, enzymes or microorganisms to loosen lignin-hemicellulose bonds.
svc.substrat_hazirlama.item4: Co-digestion: blending with manure or food waste for a balanced feed.
svc.substrat_hazirlama.item5: Homogenisation and moisture adjustment: a steady, well-mixed feed into the digester.
svc.substrat_hazirlama.faq.q1: Can biogas be produced from straw?
svc.substrat_hazirlama.faq.a1: Yes, but lignin-rich feedstocks such as straw are hard to break down. They need suitable pre-treatment and often co-digestion with another feedstock such as manure.
svc.substrat_hazirlama.faq.a2: The fibrous structure makes it hard for microorganisms to reach the organic matter. Pre-treatment opens that structure, speeds up breakdown and reduces problems such as floating layers and blockages in the digester.
svc.substrat_hazirlama.faq.q3: Which pre-treatment method should be used?
svc.substrat_hazirlama.faq.a3: It depends on the type and quantity of feedstock and the plant's energy balance. At most plants, mechanical size reduction is the first and most basic step.
svc.mikro_orc.title: Micro-ORC: Electricity from Waste Heat
svc.mikro_orc.lead: Small-scale systems that convert unused low-temperature waste heat from CHP engines and processes into electricity with an Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC).
svc.mikro_orc.item1: Waste heat analysis: assessing engine exhaust, jacket water and process heat by quantity and temperature.
svc.mikro_orc.item2: System selection: choosing a micro-ORC unit that suits the heat source and the plant's own heat demand.
svc.mikro_orc.item3: Integration: connection to the heat distribution line, the cooling system and the electrical infrastructure.
svc.mikro_orc.item4: Automation: linking the ORC unit to the plant control system and remote monitoring.
svc.mikro_orc.item5: Heat priority: using the remaining heat after needs such as digester heating and drying are met.
svc.mikro_orc.faq.a1: The Organic Rankine Cycle uses an organic fluid that evaporates at a low temperature, instead of water, to generate electricity from low- and medium-temperature heat.
svc.mikro_orc.faq.a2: Biogas and industrial plants with unused waste heat that cannot be sold or used on site.
svc.mikro_orc.faq.q3: Should waste heat go to drying or to ORC?
svc.mikro_orc.faq.a3: The plant's own heat demand comes first. Whether the remaining heat is worth more for drying or for electricity is decided by the heat balance and an economic assessment.
svc.teknik_danismanlik.title: Feasibility and Technical Consulting
svc.teknik_danismanlik.lead: Independent engineering support at every stage of a biogas investment: feasibility before the investment decision, technology selection during construction, audits and improvements in operation.
svc.teknik_danismanlik.item1: Technical feasibility: feedstock potential, mass and energy balance, capacity selection and investment assessment.
svc.teknik_danismanlik.item2: Technology and equipment selection: anaerobic digestion technology, gas storage and treatment options.
svc.teknik_danismanlik.item3: Permitting and regulatory support: compliance with environmental, safety and energy regulations.
svc.teknik_danismanlik.item4: Waste management planning: feedstock logistics and digestate use.
svc.teknik_danismanlik.item5: Operational audits: performance monitoring, troubleshooting and improvement recommendations.
svc.teknik_danismanlik.faq.q1: How much feedstock do I need for a biogas plant?
svc.teknik_danismanlik.faq.a1: There is no single number: it depends on the feedstock type, its dry matter content and the target capacity. In the feasibility study we calculate the quantity and gas potential of your waste and recommend a suitable capacity.
svc.teknik_danismanlik.faq.q2: What does a feasibility report contain?
svc.teknik_danismanlik.faq.a2: Feedstock analysis, mass and energy balance, the proposed capacity and technology, a layout concept, investment and operating costs, and a revenue estimate.
svc.teknik_danismanlik.faq.q3: Can I hire you for consulting only?
svc.teknik_danismanlik.faq.a3: Yes. We also work as independent technical consultants on projects where another company builds the plant.
